slots.title: Jobless claims at 197,000, lowest since 1969
slots.body:
Initial jobless claims: **197,000** for the week ended Sept. 26.

That is the lowest level cited in coverage going back to **1969**, per Labor Department figures summarized in the press.

The same reporting contrasts that with a soft September payrolls picture: fewer people losing jobs quickly, but companies still not adding many workers.

Treasury yields in the latest FMP snapshot (Oct. 2): **10-year at 5.3%**, **2s10s spread at 0.45** — the gap between short- and long-term government borrowing costs.

How are you weighing “few layoffs” against “slow hiring” in your read of the labor market?

slots.title: Factory input costs gauge up to 77.9
slots.body:
ISM Manufacturing **Prices Paid**: **77.9** in September, from **71.1** in August.

That is roughly a **9%** one-month increase in the survey of what U.S. factories paid for inputs.

The index measures price pressure in the supply chain — not consumer inflation (CPI), but what producers say they are paying now.

Gold futures in the session snapshot: **$4,162.30**, **-1.0%** on the day.

WTI proxy $USO: **$147.37**, **-1.8%**.

Does a jump in factory input prices change how you read the next inflation reports?

slots.title: G7 may release up to 100M barrels
slots.body:
G7 members are discussed as coordinating a release of **up to 100 million barrels** of oil and fuel.

Bloomberg Economics commentary in the clip frames that as **near-term** relief for record diesel prices.

The same segment notes limits: supply constraints linked to the **Iran war** and **attacks on Russian refining capacity** are not fully solved by stock releases.

Brent in the data: **$102.25**, **-0.1%**.

Brent day range: **$98.43** low to **$103.05** high.

Separately, Reuters reported **fire and smoke** near an **Aramco** facility in **Riyadh** on Saturday, per a witness account.

What do you watch first on energy — strategic releases or headlines from producing regions?
